exp.step.average#1|ErdosProblems.Erdos25.annotation: Take `u` to be the selected `displacementAtom` family at $b=2$. Each column is summable, giving `hu`. `tsum_progressionMean` then equates the sum of row means with the mean of column sums, with the sides reversed from Equation (4).

exp.incomplete-remove-entries|Erdos24925.annotation: The proof includes `Finset.range (N % h)` in the full block `Finset.range h`, then applies `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg` using `hx0`. This is the removal step in the argument for the separate $2Q/n$ estimate in Equation (6).

exp.appendix.add-row-averages|Erdos24925.annotation: `tsum_cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul` interchanges the infinite row sum and finite average for shifted atoms. For $K>0$ each mean subtracts the same unshifted contribution, giving the fractional-part version in Equation (4).

exp.appendix.other-bases-conclusion|Erdo.annotation: The general base `b` is a parameter of the formal conclusion. `hA` requires infinitely many exponents and `hsum` requires their reciprocals to be summable. This is a statement-level link to the all-base result in Theorem A.1 of the short paper.

exp.formal.integer-gap|Erdos249257.irrat.annotation: The integer `u N - u 0` is the denominator `v` times the increase of the shifted sum. At $b=2$, $N=k$ and $v=q$, it is $qR(k)$. The local results `hgapPos` and `hgapLt` put it strictly between $0$ and $1$ (Equation (1)).

p1-p06.notation-selected-support|Erdos24.annotation: The positive exponents selected by the real greedy rule for target $x$. An exponent $m$ belongs exactly when `m ≠ 0` and $w_m\le r_{m-1}(x)$. This uses the remainder before processing $m$, which explains the subtraction by one in the Lean expression. For $x=1/2$ it gives the paper's $G$. For a nonnegative target, Theorem 1.11 gives the exact survival test: at every rank the remainder must not exceed the sum of all later weights.

p1-p06.scope.table.factorial|Erdos249257.annotation: For every integer base $b\ge2$, the series with exponent sequence $1!,2!,3!,\ldots$ is irrational. The assumption is `hb : 2 ≤ b`. Lean writes the exponents as `Nat.factorial (k + 1)`. This is a concrete application of Theorem 6.17, which applies when the gap between the next exponent and the least common multiple of all preceding exponents tends to infinity. Beginning at $1!$ avoids the duplicate exponent that would arise from including both $0!$ and $1!$ in an indexed sum.

p1-p06.geometry.irrational-tail-reason|E.annotation: Every full Mersenne tail $R_n$ is irrational. The base case is the irrationality of $E=R_0$ (Theorem 6.14). Passing from $R_n$ to $R_{n+1}$ subtracts the rational weight $w_{n+1}$, which preserves irrationality. The declaration quantifies over all natural $n$. This is the ingredient that rules out equality between a finite rational greedy residual and a tail boundary.

p1-p06.inputs.3.2.seed-six|Erdos249257.e.annotation: There is an exact quotient row at depth six, witnessed in the proof by the support $\{2,3,6\}$. Its quotient sum is $2^5-1=31$, with all selected exponents in $\{2,\ldots,6\}$. The helper declarations immediately above give the finite arithmetic and show that its real prefix value is below one half. This is a finite starting example. A seed at one endpoint does not prove the exact rows at unbounded depths required in the compactness argument of Theorem 6.67.

p2-long.thm-frozen-margin#1.conditional-.annotation: Consumes condition (i) of Theorem 6.13. The equivalence supplies condition (ii). If the full-shell margin is nonnegative at every real greedy skipped rank from $3$ onward, then $1/2\in\mathcal A$.

p2-long.record-257bm-c2#1|Erdos249257.co.annotation: Arbitrarily late positive skips of the half-greedy rule yield exact quotient rows at unbounded depths. The only input is `hskips : CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips`. A skip at rank $c\ge4$ provides an exact row at depth $2c-2$ by Theorem 6.78, so unbounded skipped ranks give unbounded row depths. The theorem proves this implication. It does not establish the required skips. The separate half-membership equivalences explain why the antecedent remains an unresolved existence condition.

p2-long.record-257bm-c4#1|Erdos249257.co.annotation: The critical quotient supply implies exact rows at unbounded depths. Its input is `hcap : SkippedCoreCriticalQuotientSupply`, a universal inequality for finite cores at critical crossings. The proof iterates a construction from the depth-six seed and shows that the row depths increase. It does not prove `hcap`. A separate equivalence identifies this supply with the inequality along the actual skipped half-greedy prefixes (the form stated in Theorem 6.72), which is why that reduced condition can be used here.

p2-long.record-257bm-i7#1.2|Erdos249257..annotation: A below-half exact row at $n\ge6$ extends to an exact row at $2n-1$, with all new ranks above $n$. The source explicitly assumes `htwo : 2 ∈ D` as well as `hD`, `hquot` and `hbelow`, and rank-two membership follows separately for exact rows (Proposition 6.96). The conclusion preserves the quotient identity and support inclusion, but does not state that the extended row remains below $1/2$.

p2-long.record-257bm-i-bridge#1.2|Erdos2.annotation: The divisor count associated with any support satisfies $c_A(n)\le n$. The theorem quantifies over every support `A` and natural index `n`, with the zero convention included. Each selected positive divisor is among the integers from one to $n$. This uniform bound allows the generic binary-tail and integer-recurrence criterion for rationality (Theorem 6.105) to be applied to Mersenne support series.

p2-long.record-257bm-k1#1.3|ErdosProblem.annotation: There exists a predicate with a depth-six seed and the stated doubling-or-return closure property that fails cofinality. The theorem existentially quantifies over the predicate rather than over Mersenne supports. It demonstrates that those logical premises alone cannot prove arbitrarily large depths. A proof for the arithmetic problem must use further information, such as an invariant that forces returned endpoints to increase (Section 12.4.1 gives a conditional induction using an unproved capacity bound).

p2-long.prop-finite-approximations-witho.annotation: Every supplied shared-prefix family at depth $N$ contains a finite word whose terminal half-carry has absolute value at most $B(N)$. The argument `S : CylinderStage K N` includes the full family conditions, not only agreement of a few bits. The conclusion also normalizes the zero and one coordinates to false. This extracts a witness from a given family. It does not produce families at new depths (Proposition 12.4 requires terminal-strip witnesses at unbounded depths).

p2-b.twenty-one-closed-decay|Erdos249257.annotation: Closed quotient rows along depths tending to infinity imply the scaled-decay condition for the target $1/21$. The inputs are `hR : Tendsto R atTop atTop` and `hrow`, which requires $R(k)\ge2$ and remainder at most $2^{R(k)}$ at each selected depth. The conclusion is `TwentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyDecay`, not membership itself. A separate theorem consumes this condition to prove membership (Equation (16) bounds the difference between the scaled remainder and the finite subseries value error). The closed rows are assumed. This declaration does not supply them.

p2-iv.scale.skipped-survival|Erdos249257.annotation: The value $1/2$ belongs to the Mersenne achievement set exactly when its greedy procedure has no last skipped rank. The negated existential uses `IsLastHalfGreedySkip`, which includes both an actual skipped rank and the assertion that every later rank is taken. Together with the survival test at skipped ranks, this connects Table 2’s membership claim to the more local condition that each skipped remainder stays below its complete tail.

p2-long.thm-tr-finite-decision#1|ErdosPr.annotation: For a fixed $J\ge2$, a representation of $1/2$ under the truncated weights exists exactly when the greedy rule avoids fatal gaps at ranks $2$ through its decision horizon $B(J)$. The binder `hJ` is the only external hypothesis. Larger ranks are excluded as fatal gaps by the witness exclusion in Theorem 8.6 and the half-LCM horizon. The theorem supplies the finite reduction. It does not itself list the successful truncations $3\le J\le22$.

p2-iv.membership.centered-equivalence|Er.annotation: For the specific greedy support of one half, membership is equivalent to the upper bound $\operatorname{mchc}(G,N)\le2\sqrt N+4$ at every rank. The proof obtains the required inequalities from the greedy construction itself. The statement is specific to $G$ and is not an equivalence for arbitrary supports. An upper bound for a general support need only force its sum to be at least one half (the residual in Lemma 2.4 may have either sign).

p2-v12.capacity-canonical|Erdos249257.sk.annotation: The universal critical-crossing capacity condition is equivalent to its restriction to actual skipped prefixes of the half-greedy construction. The statement has no additional assumptions. Its reverse direction uses the rigidity of a critical-crossing core (Proposition 2.2(ii)), which identifies that core with the corresponding greedy prefix. Thus the restricted condition is a genuine equivalent formulation, rather than a presumed weakening based only on fewer visible quantifiers. Neither side of the equivalence is proved to hold here.

p2-v13.log-cost|ErdosProblems.Erdos257.P.annotation: `kappaOne` is `sInf (logMajorantCosts F t)`, the infimum of the costs of admissible logarithmic majorants. Writing a minimum in Equation (17) additionally requires a coefficient family attaining that infimum.

p2-v.sources.1|Erdos249257.erdos257_fami.annotation: The reciprocal Mersenne sum over exponents $(k+1)!$ is irrational. This source statement is an unconditional instance with no supplied support hypotheses. Its exponents are factorials, and they are not a pairwise-coprime sequence. The instance belongs with the least-common-multiple gap method, as the support table in Section 1.8 records. The supplementary list's label “Pairwise-coprime supports” should therefore not be read as the hypothesis behind this particular theorem.

short.front.main-result|ErdosProblems.Er.annotation: `hE` applies the weighted condition to $E$ at base two. The cover input `D : LogBudgetCover V` has positive weights and finite total cost and includes the dyadic cover after conversion. Irrationality then holds for every infinite $A\subseteq E\cup V$ at each integer base $b\ge2$ (Theorem 4.1).

short.front.incomparability|ErdosProblem.annotation: The witness has `FinitePrimeWeighted 2 A` but fails `HasStrengthenedPositiveCover A`. These two conjuncts place it in the weighted class and outside the stated divisor-cover class (Proposition 5.1).

short.w.binary-hypothesis|ErdosProblems..annotation: Set `b` to $2$ in `primeWeightedTerm` to obtain the summand in condition (W). Its sum over $A$ is finite under the separate weighted hypothesis.

short.w.astar-irrational|ErdosProblems.E.annotation: The second conjunct applies to every positive weighted support. The preceding summability calculation (worked out in Section 2.1) instantiates it at $A_\star$.

short.front.incomparable-criteria|ErdosP.annotation: There exists an infinite positive support satisfying the binary finite-prime weighted condition but admitting no cover satisfying condition (V). This declaration gives the $E$ witness for one direction of class incomparability. The other existential declaration gives the reverse direction.

There exists an infinite positive squarefree support with a cover satisfying condition (V), divergent reciprocal mass, and no finite-prime weighted condition at any integer base $b\ge2$. This declaration gives the $V$ witness for one direction of class incomparability. The other existential declaration gives the reverse direction.

step.displacement_identity#1|ErdosProble.annotation: This theorem gives the first atom-sum equality for integer $b\ge2$. It does not state the explicit $J$ double sum or the second equality in Equation (D).

step.incidence#1|Erdos249257.supportCoef.annotation: `supportCoeff` filters `n.divisors` by membership in $A$ and takes the cardinality. These counts are finite even for infinite $A$. The second equality in Equation (6) uses a separate Lambert series identity.

step.cover_condition#1|ErdosProblems.Erd.annotation: The source uses `j + 1` in the exponent because its cover sequence starts at $0$ and the paper starts at $1$. The corresponding `Summable` condition is exactly condition (V).

short.c.cover-class|ErdosProblems.Erdos2.annotation: The property that a support $A$ lies inside the union of some `PositiveCoverData` whose total cost satisfies condition (V). It quantifies over one complete sequence of finite sets, exponents and majorants. The finite sets may overlap, and their union may contain exponents outside $A$. This is the paper's class $\mathcal C$, and failure of one proposed cover does not establish that $A$ is outside this class.

short.c.exponential-minimum|ErdosProblem.annotation: For $u>0$, the inequality $eu\le e^u$ holds. The binder `_hu` states positivity. Dividing by $u$ gives $e^u/u\ge e$, the form printed in the proof of Equation (7). Substituting $u=\alpha\log t$ is valid when $t>1$ and $\alpha>0$. This is a scalar inequality, and averaging divisor counts requires the separate cover-majorant argument.

short.c.no-cover-from-growth|ErdosProble.annotation: The result excludes all arbitrary-positive-weight covers whenever finite logarithmic means are unbounded, and dyadic covers satisfying condition (V) are a special case.

short.r.finite-half-impossibility|ErdosP.annotation: The source rules out a finite positive support of value $1/2$, since the reduced denominator of a finite Mersenne sum is odd (Theorem B.1). Applying it to a support supplied by closedness establishes the infinitude claimed in the prose.

short.r.choose-terminal-one|Erdos249257..annotation: Every nonempty selected family contains a finite support satisfying the terminal approximation bound. The hypothesis `hR : 1 ≤ R` guarantees that the member with terminal carry $1$ is present. The proof chooses precisely that member and carries over its admissibility and terminal equation. It uses neither a shared prefix nor the consecutive-suffix condition. Those additional constraints may matter for constructing families, but not for this compactness step. Theorem D.2 uses this scaled error when witnesses occur at unbounded depths.

short.r.rational-skip-question|Erdos2492.annotation: The source proves an equivalence between membership and cofinal skips for nonnegative rational targets. This display is the skip condition requested in the open Problem D.4, not an asserted existence theorem. The scaled inequality is an algebraic restatement.

short.e.product-upper-bound|ErdosProblem.annotation: Lean bounds $q^{-1}\prod_{p\in P}(1+z/p)$ by $\exp(zS)/q$. The display divides by $z$ and specializes to $z=1/S$. It also calls this a cover cost, which uses the separate cube-majorant construction (expanding into nonnegative divisor indicators; see the four-exponent example in Section 3.1).
